newsitem.title: CONGO: Political factions clash in northern Congo.
newsitem.headline: Political factions clash in northern Congo.

text.p: Armed factions in Congo, Zaire's neighbour, clashed in a northern town at the weekend as politicals rivals manoeuvred ahead of July's presidential election, state radio reported on Sunday.

Armed supporters of former Marxist military leader Denis Sassou-Nguesso and former president and prime minister Jacques Joachim Yhombi-Opango fought on Saturday in Owando, 600 km (375 miles), north of the capital Brazzaville, the radio added.
Details of casualties were not immediately known but 300 paramilitary gendarmes were being despatched to Owando, it said.

Sassou Nguesso, beaten by incumbent President Pascal Lissouba in the 1992 elections, has spent the past month in the north as part of an undeclared campaign for next July's presidential polls. He has not yet officially said he will run.
Yhombi-Opango, a former general who was head of state before Sassou-Ngessou, is from the Owando region.
About a dozen candidates are expected to contest the elections. The three front-runners are Lissouba, Sassou Nguesso and Bernard Kolelas, 1992 runner-up and mayor of Brazzaville.

The last presidential election, the first multi-party poll since independence from France in 1960, left ethnic and political divisions which resulted in clashes between political militias that killed 2,000 people in Brazzaville in 1993.
Political and diplomatic sources say Lissouba could seek to postpone the July elections if the civil war in Zaire spills across the border by causing an exodus of refugees.
Brazzaville and Kinshasa, Zaire's capital, are separated by the Zaire river.
